chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Anbasah ibn Bijad al-Abid, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

We were in his presence, and they mentioned the authority of the Umayyads. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'No one rises against Hisham except that he is killed.' He also mentioned that his rule would last for twenty years. We were distressed by this. He said: 'What is the matter with you? When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intends to destroy the authority of a people, He commands the Angel, who hastens the pace of the orbit, so he gains control over what He intends to.'

We said to Zayd (peace be upon him): 'This is the discussion we had.' He said: 'I witnessed Hisham, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was insulted in his presence, yet he neither denied it nor changed it. By Allah, even if there were no one but myself and my son, I would rise against him.'

key_terms.سَيْر الْفَلَك: The pace of the orbit (celestial movement)

ai.seo_question: Why did Zayd ibn Ali decide to rebel against Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik despite the prediction of failure?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the strategic patience of Imam al-Baqir (as) during the Umayyad era, contrasting his cautious approach with the active rebellion of Zayd ibn Ali. The Imam’s reference to the 'hastening of the orbit' (sir al-falak) illustrates the divine mechanism of maintaining political stability for a ruler until the appointed time for their downfall. Zayd’s justification, rooted in Hisham’s silence during the Prophet’s insults, underscores the Shia criterion for legitimacy and the readiness to rise even with limited forces when justice is suppressed.
